blocks.text: Restart policies restart a container when its PID 1 exits; they never react to health status.

rows: Starts again when the daemon restarts

items: Backoff starts at 100 ms and doubles per consecutive failure; it resets after ~10 s of uptime.
Applies only after one successful start: create-time failures (bad mount, port allocated) aren't retried.
A restart reuses the same container, writable layer and env.
`--restart` conflicts with `--rm`; change it live with `docker update --restart`.
Migrations and one-shots: `no` (with `always`, a migration reruns forever).

blocks.text: An unhealthy HEALTHCHECK doesn't restart anything in Docker or Compose. A hung-but-alive process stays up; Swarm and Kubernetes liveness probes are what act on health.

Q: "always vs unless-stopped?" A: "Both restart on any exit and after daemon restarts, but unless-stopped remembers a manual docker stop and stays down, while always starts the container again when the daemon restarts."

items: Policies react to exits, not health.
unless-stopped for services; no for one-shots.
Crash loops hide causes: read logs and RestartCount.
